[h1]While it’s not L4D3, it’s still a great, quality cooperative zombie horde shooter with its own charm.[/h1] 

Valve’s inability to count to 3 caused many of their fans to look for alternatives. The co-op zombie shooter market wasn’t really dead, it’s just that the genre itself dispersed and moved on in different directions. There were Dead Islands and Dying Lights with more emphasis on melee combat and more focused storytelling, sandboxish Dead Rising series or survival games like DayZ or 7 Days to Die. 
Back 4 Blood decided to take a more classic approach, with hordes constantly on your heels, special infected out for your butt, the game director and rushing to the saferoom at the end of every level. 

The plot starts out in a post-apocalyptic world infested with “The Ridden”, which are basically zombies controlled by some weird parasitic worms. What’s kind of interesting is that the initial “fall of humanity” took place earlier and the characters actually say that they haven’t seen a single ridden for quite some time now. 
...Which doesn’t matter because they just get attacked by them anyway and they’re back. The team retreats to Fort Hope (I like the name honestly), then goes to find a bioweapon to counter the monsters, clean zombie hives, fight a big zombie toad at the end and just shoot an unreasonable amount of ammunition throughout the whole ordeal (and fight a zombie cult if you bought the DLCs). 
Now the plot of this game is nothing special, nor should it really, because it’s not the focus of the game. There is value in the individual playable characters though. With time they’ve grown on me. They all have unique characters, attitudes, even little snippets of backstories that aren’t shoved down your throat or anything, but told casually during the map progression on random. 

My favorite thing about the gameplay is actually the gunplay. There is a broad selection of weaponry, both firearms and melee weapons. The guns just feel good to shoot and have nice animations (I like the angle when you crouch). There are a lot of attachments to them and cosmetics to unlock. 
Every character has passive abilities that you can utilize during the game. Doc is better at healing, Walker gives buffs for spotting enemies, Evangelo is a good runner, able to break from grabs. 
The special infected are... alright. Their main thing is to shoot them at their weak points to kill them faster. There are of course fat dudes vomiting goo on you, skinny gremlins firing stings at you and tall dudes crushing you with their arms. There are bosses too, the most interesting is the Hag that runs around and if it runs into you or you startle it, it’s just going to eat you like a glizzy and insta kill you (I platinumed this game and I still have no idea how to deal with her).
The problem with these enemies is that they are really tanky. A boomer in L4D would pop almost instantly, everything here needs at least half a clip, even on the weak points on higher difficulties. 
Before each map, you get a little shop that offers passive upgrades, supplies, grenades or weapons with attachments. You pay with copper that you collect during maps and earn through side objectives. Spend it wisely, because first aid kits use it to heal trauma damage (unhealable with anything else).
The general gameplay is really cool, but the game is more complicated. I understand that this was ideally supposed to be L4D3, improved with new things and mechanics, but L4D’s thing was that it was quite simple. You jump into the game after like 2 years, with your buds, whatever map, enter and go. You didn’t need to remember how things worked. Back 4 Blood has several types of health, the whole card system shaping your build and the current level, many tools and healing items doing different things (because which healing item heals this particular type of health?) and all this can be upgraded with copper and stuff. 
Don’t get me wrong, these mechanics are interesting, good to utilize and fun to learn. I’m just pointing out that there is just a lot of stuff here. The game encourages communication and working together.
Regarding the card system though. You unlock these, put them in your deck and and this shapes your playstyle. It’s a fun thing to experiment with. The levels themselves have their own random cards, that make every playthrough different and can drastically change how you need to approach the map. You can also buy additional buff cards with copper when you find intel files.
DLCs unlock Hives, which are a good way to get better supplies during the campaign, skip some harder sections in the level if you’re lucky or get skull totems which are a new currency. Besides that, they unlock 2 brand new shorter campaigns involving a worm-loving cult. 
Only one person in the party must have the DLC for everyone to play them, which is cool. 

Game looks pretty, has a nice bloody aesthetic and monster designs are okay. One thing that is annoying is characters covered in blood during the chaos and carnage are indistinguishable from the zombies, so you constantly commit friendly fire. Also, very good and communicative sound design.

As a side note though - I don't think this game was ever so competetive that it needed [b]a kernel level anti-cheat software[/b]. That is a big minus, and a big nuh-uh, and just keep that in mind while installing it.

While it’s not L4D3 it’s a great game in its own right. The player count diminished, but it’s a quality production even solo. If you’re looking for something to play with your buds and pop undead heads, that’s the game.
